name: Right Brigade
label: Revelation
lede: Boston straight edge kids from Fastbreak and Follow Through played SSD-style hardcore, sold over a thousand demos locally, and ended up on Revelation with a bio calling them the biggest band in hardcore.

eras.title: Over a thousand demos, sold in Boston
eras.text: Right Brigade came out of Boston's late-'90s straight edge scene, with members from Fastbreak and Follow Through. Their reference point sat behind youth crew, back with SSD and Negative FX.

years.h: Patrick Rorick, Fastbreak's singer, switches to guitar
years.p: In Right Brigade Rorick plays guitar and writes much of the music, per Lollipop Magazine. Brian "Clevo" Ristau is on Revelation's roster page.

years.h: The self-released demo sells over 1,000 copies in Boston
years.p: Right Brigade press up a demo themselves, and Last.fm's bio says it moves more than 1,000 copies locally.

eras.title: Revelation catalog number 101
eras.text: Revelation released the band's one album as REV 101: fourteen songs of powerchords and mosh parts, closing on a title borrowed from Hemingway.

years.h: REV 101: fourteen songs, closing on a Hemingway line
years.p: Right Brigade runs from Broken to Isn't It Pretty To Think So?, the last line of The Sun Also Rises. The first pressing is 317 red and 775 black.
years.xp: Revelation lists the record as catalog number 101. The same Boston scene is on tape at Davis Square on April 20, 2001, on a bill with Bane, American Nightmare and Carry On.

years.h: Revelation's page bills them as hardcore's biggest band
years.p: The label's own band page is a straight-faced joke. It calls Ristau the maestro of the mosh part and says the band stopped when producers of "Moon Landing" questioned the song No Way.
years.xp:
The page's interview with Ristau keeps the deadpan. On being edge: "I am edge. Period." Asked where he'd be without punk and hardcore, he says "Fucking nowhere."

He says he liked having a say from the start in Right Brigade, unlike joining Ten Yard Fight as a replacement, and names the Misfits, Murphy's Law and 7 Seconds as influences.

years.h: Lollipop hears early Fastbreak, only tougher
years.p: Reviewing Right Brigade, Tim Den calls it heavy-handed, old-school hardcore in all but name, and credits guitarist Rorick as the likely main songwriter.
years.xp: Den liked that one song aims at the scene's casual crowd. His warning: newcomers might not tell Right Brigade from a hundred other hardcore bands.

eras.title: A second life on a Bridge 9 comp
eras.text: The recordings resurfaced on a collection from another Boston label.

years.h: Bridge 9 collects them on a singles comp, Vol. 2
years.p: Right Brigade appear on Singles Collection, Vol. 2, from Boston's Bridge 9 Records.
